included_processes: DNA polymerase alpha adding a short DNA fragment to the RNA primer
lagging-strand Okazaki fragment synthesis by DNA polymerase delta
displacement and removal of primer RNA by RNase H (flap endonuclease) on the lagging strand
sealing of remaining gaps by DNA ligase
excluded_processes: origin recognition and pre-replication complex assembly
helicase unwinding and topoisomerase supercoiling relief
leading-strand continuous synthesis by DNA polymerase epsilon
simplifications: The model depicts one local lagging-strand region; strand geometry and fork movement are not modeled.
Polymerase hand-off after pol alpha is shown as a sequential process, not as a molecular mechanism.
The 'sliding clamp (PCNA)' is omitted as a separate entity because its exact mechanistic role is not needed for the described local maturation event.
RNase H and flap endonuclease are treated as the same activity as stated in the source.

support.quote: Primers are formed by the enzyme primase, and using the primer, DNA pol can start synthesis.
Primers are formed by the enzyme primase, and using the primer, DNA pol can start synthesis.
DNA pol α adds a short (20 to 30 nucleotides) DNA fragment to the RNA primer on both strands, and then hands off to a second polymerase.
While the leading strand is continuously synthesized by the enzyme pol ε , the lagging strand is synthesized by pol δ .
The displaced primer RNA is then removed by RNase H (AKA flap endonuclease ) and replaced with DNA nucleotides.
The gaps that remain are sealed by DNA ligase, which forms the phosphodiester bond.

unresolved_questions.question: Exact mechanism of polymerase hand-off from pol alpha to pol delta is not specified in the source.
Whether RNase H and flap endonuclease are distinct activities in this context is ambiguous in the source.
The source does not state whether primer removal and DNA replacement occur simultaneously or sequentially.
The number of nucleotides added by pol delta before encountering the next primer is not specified.
